approval_source.question_set: How staging comes back after the double sign in the validator recovery drill of 10 November 2026, and whether the forked validator disk is kept before it is wiped

reason: During the validator recovery drill on dytallix-staging-2 (10 November 2026), the sentry failed to start and the replacement validator, alone and the only validator, signed heights 1 to 1,401 of a fork with the key that had signed the real chain to 173,074. The fork stayed on the replacement. The causes and the fixes (#134, #136, #137, #138) are in the incident record.

decisions.question: How staging comes back
Whether the forked validator disk is kept before it is wiped
decisions.rule: A provider snapshot of the replacement's disk is taken and seen available first. It holds the forked blocks and the signing state at 1,401, and it is kept: retired, never deleted. Then validator-1 is reinstalled to the bare operating system, so the forked signing state can never start again. Its delete and rebuild protection is turned back on.

accepted_risks: The staging chain stays down until dytallix-staging-3 is installed, so no staging run can happen in between.

Several items stay open and are listed in the incident record: the startup budget, the startup check's scope, the sentry archive, 4 GB staging hosts, Restart=no, catch-up through consensus against the 6-hour objective, and watching the sentry after the validator starts.
does_not_authorize: installing dytallix-staging-3, or reinstalling the sentry
running the validator recovery drill again
